This chapter describes how snapy fills the ghost cells of a block and how it treats immersed solids. Three
mechanisms share that job and are kept apart throughout: the physical face callbacks that a block installs
from its YAML card (reflecting, periodic, extrapolation, outflow, custom, solid), the layout exchange that
fills the ghosts a neighbouring block owns, and the solid mask that closes fluid faces inside the block. The
chapter derives, for each callback, the discrete identity it implements (parity, permutation, constant
extension, characteristic selection and admissibility), the ownership rule that decides which of the two
fillers writes a ghost and when, the line optimum of the mask rectification, the reflecting closure of the
implicit system against a solid, and the wall continuation of the hydrostatic reference. Every claim is read
from the code at the pin named in each scheme's provenance block; no solver run is reported here, and the
solver tests the schemes cite are catalogued, with their assertions, in @sec-ch15-ch11.

@fig-ch11-opening-dependencies shows which scheme needs which. The complete switch matrix is
@sec-ch12-matrix; the stage ownership map is @sec-ch01-stage.
